responses.m1_analysis: My revised request improved how the task was conveyed because I specified exactly where the robot should go and what object it should inspect compared the ambiguous request. These actions fit the robot's capabilities because it has wheels and a camera. However, from the generated answer, the model basically repeated my instructions instead of creating a better detailed plan.
responses.m2_analysis: I chose the Decide task. My revised request did generate a better answer because I was specifice with what the robot needed to draw on the wooden workbench. Compared to the original where the model chose a measuring tape without knowing what the robot needed to do, my answer allowed the model to chose a compass. The photograph shows a compass with two pointed legs whcih supports the new answer.
responses.m3_analysis: I compared my improved prompt with the first prompt, "Goal only". Even though my prompt gave the robot specific waypoints and directions to follow, both experiments had the same results. My prompt did not improve the robot's navigation because it continued moving up and down instead of following the waypoints around the walls. As this was my first attempt, I learned a lot and could see a lot of improvment given time and more trials. This shows that even with seemingly clearer instructions, the model can still struggle to make correct movement decisions.
responses.final_synthesis: The three missions in this lab really taught me a lot about how hard it is to make a functioning robot. In Mission 1, I learned that being specific with instructions helps the model understand what the robot is supposed to do. If you are not, the robot just will not respond like how you would wamt it to. My improved request told the robot to navigate to the shelf, inspect the cup, report its observations, and return to base. In Mission 2, I learned that the model can make assumptions about images. For example, when I asked which tool would help draw a circle, the model suggested a compass. Although this took did make sense for the task at hand, it was not specific in explaining whether the tool was actually visible in the photograph. This showed me why we need to compare the model's claims with visual evidence. In Mission 3, I learned that even detailed movement instructions do not guarantee successful navigation. My improved prompt included specific waypoints, but the robot still failed to reach the goal. One remaining limitation is that the model can struggle to follow directions consistently, even when the instructions are clear.
responses.final.course_reflection: This lab really humbled me in what I thought I knew about robots. Normally in these labs, I would be able to do the tasks at hand just fine. However, in mission 3 of this lab where I had to give a revised prompt for the robot to reach the blue goal, I failed to even make it half way there. I was sure my specific prompt would allow the robot to understand where to go. However, my prompt was just as effective as the first unspecific prompt we tested in this mission. I was surprised at why this was and now respect these robot creators even more. This lab made me more interested in learning how robots process instructions and make decisions. It also showed me why testing is important in programming and engineering as trial and error becomes a main factor in creating a proper working robot Just because something sounds correct does not mean it will work as expected.

controls.control_adapt_instruction: Move the blue cup to the tray
controls.control_adapt_scenario: The request does not identify the intended cup
controls.control_live_language_custom_prompt: At the base, you will  navigate to the shelf and inspect the cup. Record and report what you observe about the cup. Do not pick it up. After inspecting the cup, return to the base and stop.
controls.control_live_vision_custom_prompt: A robot draws a circle on a flat wooden workbench. Examine the image. Which tool would be most useful for this task? Explain your decision by stating what features of the tool allow for doing the task. If you are unsure, explain what additional information you would need before choosing it.
controls.control_robot_custom_prompt: Starting from (1,7), we want reach the blue target at (11,1). Move UP to decrease the row, DOWN to increase the row, RIGHT to increase the column, and LEFT to decrease the column. Choose only one action per step. When you reach a waypoint, move toward the next one. Avoid walls and do not repeat blocked moves. Only choose STOP when you reach the final goal at (11,1).
